newsitem.title: USA: US WAGE PRESSURES "FOREBODING SIGN"-FED'S PHILLIPS.
newsitem.headline: US WAGE PRESSURES "FOREBODING SIGN"-FED'S PHILLIPS.

text.p: U.S. Federal Reserve board member Susan Phillips said on Thursday that signs of growing wage and salary pressures in the increasingly tight U.S. labor market could hint at the potential for higher inflation.

"We certainly are seeing pressures in certain areas and I do think that (with) as tight a labor market as we have, that is a foreboding sign in terms of the potential for inflationary increases," she told Reuters in an interview.
However, Phillips said there was no sign of those pressures having fed through into higher inflation rates yet.
She added that government reports that U.S. economic growth had slowed to 2.2 percent in the second quarter of this year from 4.9 percent in the first three months were "comforting."
"That provided some relief," she said, adding that the economy overall was doing "really quite well."
Fed policy makers have said they generally expect economic growth to slow to 2 to 2.5 percent next year from between 3 and 3.25 percent this year.
